findings.issue: Enum violation. The `conforms_to_standard` slot is a `DataStandardEnum` whose permitted values are DICOM, BIDS, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, CDS, RO_CRATE, FHIR, OTHER. The top-level list contains `DICOM` (valid) but the schema digest lists `CDS` and `RO_CRATE` as permitted, so those are fine; however the list as written is valid on every member. Re-checked: DICOM, CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE are all permitted. No violation at the top level. Withdrawn.

`affiliations` has range `Organization[]`, and the object supplied carries only `name: AI-READI Consortium`. The AI-READI Consortium is the creator itself (FAIRhub DataCite: creatorName 'AI-READI Consortium', nameType 'Organizational'), not an affiliation of a creator. The record models one organizational creator as an affiliation attached to an unnamed creator whose only substantive field is `principal_investigator`. The bundle supports a single organizational creator; the current shape misplaces it.

Aaron Lee is named in the bundle as principal investigator of the study, not as a creator of the dataset; the FAIRhub creator list contains only the organization. Attaching him under `Creator.principal_investigator` is defensible, but the accompanying `source_caveats` text about the affiliation conflict is trust commentary correctly placed in `source_caveats` — no defect there. Flagged only because the surrounding Creator object has no `name`-bearing organization of its own.

Range is `string` and the value 'AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0' is supported, but the bundle's tier-1 FAIRhub `rights` block gives `rightsName: 'AI-READI custom license v2.0'` while the license PDF titles itself 'AI-READI DATA LICENSE AGREEMENT (Version 2.0)'. Two tier-1/tier-2 renderings of the same name differ and no `source_caveats` records the divergence.

Range is `uriorcurie`. The value `https://fairhub.io/` is a bare website URL, not an identifier for the publishing organization, and it duplicates the landing-page host already carried in `page`. The bundle supplies `publisherName: 'FAIRhub'` (tier-1 FAIRhub DataCite) with no registry identifier for FAIRhub itself; no declared prefix covers it. A resolver URL is acceptable as the `uri` half of `uriorcurie` only where no prefix fits, which holds here, but the trailing-slash root URL is a weak identifier.

`ROR:01yc7t268` is correctly CURIE-form for a `uriorcurie` and the ROR is stated in the bundle (FAIRhub managingOrganization and leadSponsor both give https://ror.org/01yc7t268 for Washington University in St. Louis). Conforms; noted only to confirm the identifier is attested rather than supplied from outside the bundle.

Internal inconsistency between sibling fields within one object. `subpopulation_elements_present: false` is asserted while `distribution` enumerates race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes-status counts for the same participants. The `source_caveats` field explains the tension, but the boolean still contradicts the populated `distribution`. Either the boolean should reflect that aggregate subpopulation counts are documented, or the aggregate counts belong under `splits.split_details` (where they are already recorded) rather than duplicated here.

Two objects in the same list assert contradictory booleans (`sensitive_elements_present: false` for the public tier, `true` for the controlled tier) with no field distinguishing which release tier each describes other than the free-text `sensitivity_details`. A reader consuming only the booleans sees a direct contradiction. The dataset referent chosen elsewhere in the record is the public v3.0.0 release (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3, 'contain no protected health information'), so the second object describes a tier that is not this dataset.

The value `restricted` is inferred by the record's own reasoning ('recorded here as "restricted" because public download requires verified login...'), while the only attested value in the bundle is the RO-Crate's `confidentialityLevel: 'HL7:2N (normal)'`. The `source_caveats` discloses the substitution honestly, but the slot itself now carries a value the bundle does not state, derived rather than transcribed. `unrestricted` is not right either; the defect is that an enum value was reasoned to rather than read off.

Same pattern. `compliant` is a formal enum assertion, but the bundle states only that 'we checked that no identifiable data per US HIPAA were present in the data' and that the public set is stripped of PHI via Safe Harbor. No compliance determination or certification is stated. The `source_caveats` admits 'no formal certification is cited in the bundle', which is an argument for omitting the slot rather than populating it.

`false` is asserted while the same object's `source_caveats` records that FAIRhub sets `deIdentType: 'NoDeIdentification'` with `deIdentDirect: true`. The bundle's own detail field resolves this ('No identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary'), so `false` is the better reading, but the flag `deIdentDirect: true` in the source is not explained by the caveat as written.

`B2AI_TOPIC:43` is Diabetes, which fits. However `data_substrate` is omitted entirely despite the bundle supporting several substrate terms directly (DICOM=11, Comma-separated values=6, Waveform Data=49, Time-series data=69, Retinal Image=65, Optical coherence tomography data=67, Continuous/Glucose monitoring data=78, Physical activity data=73). `Instance` permits `data_substrate`, and the bundle names the substrates explicitly per datatype. This is a supported omission.

Only one topic term is carried on a single Instance object, but `data_topic` is single-valued on Instance, so multiple topics (Diabetes=43, Ophthalmic Imaging=24, Waveform=37, mHealth=18, Glucose Monitoring=38, Activity Monitoring=39, Environment=11) cannot all be expressed on one Instance. Not a defect in shape; noted because the single Instance flattens a deliberately multimodal dataset.

Every file_collection carries a `conforms_to_standard` list containing `CDS`. `CDS` is permitted by the enum, so this conforms. Re-checked against the digest: permitted values include `CDS`. No violation. Withdrawn.

Each collection reuses the RO-Crate subcrate ARK (e.g. `ark:59853/rocrate-b2ai-ai-readi-ecg`) as its `id`. These are attested identifiers from the bundle and are pointed at by nothing else in the record — no slot references them. Under the minting rule, an identifier for a part of this dataset is warranted only where another value points at it. Here the ids are attested rather than minted, so they are not fabricated, but they also serve no referential purpose. Acceptable but inert.

`VariableMetadata` does not declare a `description` field in the schema digest. The permitted fields are: `variable_name` (required), `categories`, `data_type`, `derivation`, `examples`, `is_identifier`, `is_sensitive`, `maximum_value`, `measurement_technique`, `minimum_value`, `missing_value_code`, `notes`, `precision`, `quality_notes`, `source_caveats`, `unit`. Every one of the eleven variable objects carries a `description` key. This is an undeclared key and will fail validation.

The `ExternalResource` class declares an `external_resources` field, and the record nests a prose blob there listing six URLs. The declared range of the inner `external_resources` is not given in the digest as a scalar string; the outer slot is `ExternalResource[]`. Packing six distinct resources into one prose string in one object collapses six entities into one, contrary to the multivalued-entity rule — each documentation site, code repository, specification and license record is a distinct external resource.

Two associated publications (Nature Metabolism and BMJ Open) are collapsed into a single `ExternalResource` prose string, and the ClinicalTrials.gov registration plus the NIH RePORTER project are appended into `notes` of the same object. Four distinct external entities in one object.

Both entries use `relationship_type: is_new_version_of` with `target_dataset` pointing at the older versions. Semantically the current dataset *is a new version of* v2.0.0, and v2.0.0 is a new version of v1.0.0 — but the record asserts that v3.0.0 is a new version of v1.0.0 directly as well. The bundle supports `is_new_version_of` v2.0.0; the v1.0.0 relation is more accurately `is_version_of` or a chained relation. Minor semantic overreach.
Supported omission is correct here — the healthsheet's erratum question was returned blank, and the record's `source_caveats` says so. No defect. Withdrawn.

Supported omission of a stated fact. The healthsheet answers the extension question explicitly: 'No, currently there is no mechanism for others to extend or augment the AI-READI dataset outside of those who are involved in the project.' `ExtensionMechanism.extension_details` can carry this. The record omits the slot entirely rather than recording the stated negative.
Supported omission. The healthsheet answers 'Has the dataset been used for any tasks already?' with 'No'. `ExistingUse` permits recording this. Omitted.
Supported omission. The healthsheet answers 'Is there a repository that links to any or all papers or systems that use the dataset?' with 'No'. Omitted rather than recorded.
Supported omission. The healthsheet states explicitly: 'No, a data protection impact analysis has not been conducted.' `DataProtectionImpact.impact_details` can carry this stated negative. Omitted.

Supported omission. The bundle states repeatedly and in a dedicated healthsheet section that no labeling was performed and no labels are provided ('N/A - no labels are provided'; RO-Crate `rai:dataAnnotationProtocol`: 'N/A - no labels are provided'). This is a labeling-strategy fact. It is currently expressed only obliquely inside `instances[0].label_description` and `tasks[2].response`.
Correctly omitted — no annotation was performed, so there is no agreement to analyze. No defect.

Borderline. `missing_data_documentation[0].handling_strategy` states 'Missing values were not imputed', which is the imputation fact. Recording it under missing-data handling is defensible; a dedicated `ImputationProtocol` with `imputation_method: 'none'` would be redundant. No repair required.

The caveat states the tier-1 FAIRhub date (19 July 2023) is preferred over the tier-3 BMJ figure (18 July 2023) and that BMJ says enrolment continues to 30 November 2026. Correct application of the ranking. However `end_date: '2025-05-01'` is the *data cut-off for this release*, not the end of collection, and the bundle states enrollment is ongoing with anticipated study completion 1 January 2027. The field name means the collection period; the value means the release window.

All omitted. The bundle supplies `created_at: 1763366400` (FAIRhub, = 2025-11-17) for the dataset record, which is already carried in `issued`. No independent creation or modification timestamp is attested. Correct omission.

Correctly omitted — no automated annotation tools were used. However the bundle does describe automated processing tooling (OMOP DQD, automated conversion pipelines, 'automated + custom' processing per the changelog). Those are preprocessing, not annotation, and are already in `preprocessing_strategies`. No defect.
Correctly omitted; the bundle names no compression format for the distribution.

Supported omission, arguably. The recommended train/validation/test partitions are recorded in `splits[0].split_details` as prose. The schema also offers `subsets` (`DataSubset[]`, `is_data_split` flag) for exactly this, with per-subset counts. The counts are given per split and per stratum in the bundle README table. Currently all of it is one prose blob.

Both omitted. The RO-Crate models the release as a parent crate with nine subcrates via `hasPart`, and each subcrate records `isPartOf` the release. That hierarchy is expressed here through `file_collections`, which the schema explicitly designates for file groupings, so `resources` is correctly avoided. `parent_datasets` is correctly empty (the RO-Crate root has `isPartOf: []`). No defect.

Left unset while the three sibling booleans are set true. The bundle's healthsheet answer addresses directly-observed and subject-reported acquisition and does not assert inference/derivation, so leaving it unset rather than false is defensible, though `false` would be the more complete reading of 'the acquisition of data varied... some data were directly observable... whereas other data were reported by subjects'.

The `notes` slot carries substantive dataset content that fitting structured slots exist for: the return-of-results procedures (exam card, Dexcom report by encrypted email, laboratory results at yearly release) and the incidental-findings referral pathway are participant-facing procedures; the UAB biorepository description names biospecimens explicitly excluded from the dataset. Per the notes rule, structured slots first, then description, notes only for residue. The 'under review for potential modification' banner and the FAIRhub beta status are genuine residue and belong here.
Well-formed and grounded. One point: it states 'No labels or annotations are provided' and 'the dataset is deliberately hypothesis-agnostic', both attested. No defect.

Item (1) reports the enrollment-target conflict (4,000 tier-1/tier-3 vs 4,600 tier-2 IRB) and states the tier-1 figure is used. Correct under the ranking. Item (4) reports the two expansions of the AI-READI acronym ('Equitable' vs 'Exploratory') but the record's own `description` uses neither expansion, so the caveat annotates a value that is not present. Minor: the caveat is accurate but orphaned.

`id` is `doi:10.60775/fairhub.3`, a CURIE in a `uriorcurie` slot — correct form. But the `doi` slot separately carries the bare `10.60775/fairhub.3` as required by its own pattern, and `related_datasets[*].target_dataset` uses `doi:10.60775/fairhub.2` and `doi:10.60775/fairhub.1`. `target_dataset` is a required key on `DatasetRelationship`; the digest does not state its range. If its range is `string` rather than `uriorcurie`, the `doi:` prefix form may be wrong there. Flagging for verification against the full schema.

`Maintainer.role` is enum-constrained to: data_subject, third_party, researcher, industry, academic_institution, government_agency, commercial_entity, non_profit_organization, crowdsourced, automated_system, other. The value `academic_institution` is permitted — conforms. However the maintainer is 'the AI-READI team', a multi-institution consortium, and no `Person` or contact is attached despite the bundle giving contact@aireadi.org and https://aireadi.org/contact. Those sit in `maintainer_details` prose instead.

`DataCollector.role` is not enum-constrained per the digest (only `Maintainer.role` is), so the free-text values 'clinical research coordinator', 'data manager', 'research assistant', 'retinal imaging technician', 'laboratory and biospecimen staff' are permissible. Conforms.

Value 'USD 200' is a string blending currency and quantity. The bundle states '$200 for the study visit'. Acceptable as free text, but note the IRB protocol (tier 2) says 'There will be a $200 stipend' and adds 'The amount may be changed in future years depending on the study funding' — a qualification the record does not carry.

Sixteen distinct mechanism objects, one per instrument class — correct application of the multivalued-entity rule. Each carries only `mechanism_details` prose, which is the only substantive field `CollectionMechanism` declares besides notes/caveats. Conforms.

'AI-READI ethics team' is not an organization named as such in the bundle. The RO-Crate field is `ethicalReview: 'Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans'` — four named individuals, not an organization. The record invents an organizational label to hold them. `EthicalReview` offers `contact_person` (range `Person`) for named individuals; four reviewers would be four objects or belong in `review_details`.

'AI-READI Community Advisory Board' is attested in the BMJ protocol ('A Community Advisory Board of 11 persons from the three sites') and in the IRB protocol ('there will also be a community advisory board that evaluates the consent forms and research protocols'). The name as given is a reasonable rendering. Low concern.

Range check. `irb_approval` is listed among the fields `HumanSubjectResearch` accepts; the digest does not state its range. The record supplies a list of one prose string. If the declared range is a scalar `string`, a list will fail validation. Flagging for verification. Same concern applies to `regulatory_compliance` and `special_populations` on the same object, all of which are supplied as single-element lists.

Same range question: supplied as a single-element list of prose. Also, the content is largely *exclusion* criteria (no minors, pregnancy excluded) plus transportation assistance — the former is eligibility, already in `known_limitations[3]`, and belongs there or in sampling; the latter is a genuine accessibility protection.

Single-element list of a long prose paragraph covering title/ownership, derivative data, synthetic data and licensee models — four distinct restrictions collapsed into one entry. If the range is a list, each restriction should be its own entry.
Same pattern: one prose entry covering the license reference, the NIH GDS Policy security requirement, the general legal-compliance clause and the storage-location restriction.

Coverage gap rather than shape defect. Eleven variables are documented from a dataset the bundle describes as spanning 'over 10 domains' with an uploaded variable list and full per-domain documentation. The eleven chosen are reasonable exemplars, but the record nowhere states that the list is illustrative rather than complete, which risks reading as the full variable inventory.

3815969779678 matches FAIRhub `size` exactly and is consistent with the '3.82 TB' string. The nine file_collection `total_bytes` sum to 3,815,974,109,064 — approximately 4.3 MB above the declared total, i.e. the per-directory sizes do not sum to the reported dataset size. Both figures come from the same tier-1 source; noting the arithmetic inconsistency, which the bundle itself contains.

356343 matches FAIRhub exactly. The nine file_collection `file_count` values sum to 356,334 — nine short of the declared total, consistent with the nine root-level metadata files (CHANGELOG.md, dataset_description.json, dataset_structure_description.json, healthsheet.md, LICENSE.txt, participants.json, participants.tsv, README.md, study_description.json). Internally coherent; no defect.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared bundle. Three findings were raised and withdrawn on re-check (conforms_to_standard enum membership at both top level and file_collections; errata omission). Remaining defects cluster in four groups. (1) Shape/schema conformance: every one of the eleven `variables` objects carries an undeclared `description` key that `VariableMetadata` does not declare and which will fail validation — this is the single highest-confidence blocker. Several single-element prose lists (`human_subject_research.irb_approval`, `regulatory_compliance`, `special_populations`, `at_risk_populations.special_protections`, `ip_restrictions.restrictions`) need their declared ranges verified against the full schema. (2) Entity collapsing: `external_resources` packs six distinct resources into one prose string in the first object and four more (two publications, a trial registration, a grant record) into the second, contrary to the one-object-per-entity rule; `creators` models the sole organizational creator as an *affiliation* of an unnamed creator rather than as the creator itself. (3) Values reasoned to rather than read off: `regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted` overrides the only attested value (RO-Crate 'HL7:2N (normal)') by the record's own argument, and `hipaa_compliant: compliant` is a formal enum assertion the bundle never makes — both disclose the substitution in `source_caveats`, which is honest but is an argument for omission rather than population. `ethical_reviews[1].reviewing_organization: 'AI-READI ethics team'` invents an organizational label to hold four named individuals the RO-Crate lists as people. (4) Supported omissions: five stated negatives in the bundle are dropped rather than recorded — no extension mechanism, no existing uses, no use repository, no data protection impact assessment, and no labeling performed. Also flagged: internal boolean/content contradictions in `subpopulations[0]` and across the two `sensitive_elements` objects (the second describes the controlled-access tier, which is not the referent this record selected); `collection_timeframes[0].end_date` records the release cut-off under a field meaning the collection period while the bundle says enrollment is ongoing to 2027; `instances[0]` omits `data_substrate` despite the bundle naming substrates explicitly per datatype; and `notes` carries return-of-results and biorepository content for which structured slots exist. Two arithmetic observations on file counts and sizes are inconsistencies present in the bundle itself, not record defects.
